newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end up as budget looms, golds firm.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end up as budget looms, golds firm.

text.p: South African shares continued their recent rally on Tuesday, ending solidly up and knocking on the door of new closing all-time highs as Wednesday's budget looms over the market, dealers said.
An overnight record on Wall Street gave a shot in the arm to most world financial centres and the Johannesburg Stock Exchange was no exception.
Shares jumped quickly in early trade and, despite a late dip, held most of their gains in healthy volumes of about 804 million rand worth of trade.
The all-share index rose 70.7 points to 7,162.0 as the industrials index added 57.7 points to 8,384.7.

All market eyes are now set to watch the budget unfold on Wednesday and the prognosis is seen as good. If finance minister Trevor Manuel delivers a market-pleasing speech dealers expect new stock market records to be set towards the end of the week.
"If all goes well, we should see some new highs," one dealer said. The all-time closing high for the all-share index stands at 7,205.67, set on February 26 earlier this year.
Markets are especially looking for steps towards the gradual phasing out of exchange controls which are expected to be modest, but psychologically important.
The issue is seen as a major impediment to investor confidence, by artificially locking unwilling capital in South African assets.
Gold shares had a firm day as the bullion price struggled upwards and held above the important $350 an ounce level, giving support to confidence in the battered sector.
The golds index put on 37.1 points, or 2.64 percent, to 1,441.4.
